newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 24.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) leader Begum Khaleda Zia has complained that the ruling Awami League resorted to oppression on political opponents to what she said divert people's attention from its inability to meet election pledges.
The government has formed a commission to suggest ways to render the local government bodies more financial and administrative power.

The government has decided not to permit any more private medical colleges for maintaining the quality of education. There are currently nine private medical colleges in the country, but only three of them have government permission. Action has been initiated against colleges without government recognition.

Opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has protested the governemnt's plan to import electricity, saying it will destroy the country's power sector. BNP, in a statement, also opposed to price hike of power.
Student wing of fundamentalist Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami party has called general strike in the port city of Chittagong on Thursday to protest police raid on the Chittagong University campus.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina asked the government officials to work with "utmost" sincerity and help her government to achieve rapid development.
The International Finnce Corporation (IFC) has decided to include the names of some 45 leading companies listed with the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) in its emerging market data base.
